metadata.note: Kansas Central Railway / Leavenworth, Kansas and Western Railway: one 165-mile line, Leavenworth (Union Station) - Valley Falls - Holton - Circleville - Onaga - Garrison - Clay Center - Miltonvale, Kansas, built 3 ft gauge 1872-1882 and later standard-gauged on the same roadbed. Passenger service 1872-1934 (last train 10 Jan 1935). Drawn as eight features sharing one trace: four Kansas Central features, one per construction stage (Leavenworth - Holton 1872, Holton - Onaga 1878, Onaga - Garrison 1880, Garrison - Clay Center 1881), each ending 1881; then whole-line features for Union Pacific 1882-1894, the court-operated Kansas Central 1895-1896, the LK&W 1897-1907, and UP's Leavenworth Western Branch 1908-1934. Research report: research/branches/leavenworth_kansas_and_western_railway.txt.
references: H. Crimmins, "A History of the Kansas Central Railway, 1871-1935", Emporia State Research Studies 2:4 (June 1954), https://dspacep01.emporia.edu/handle/123456789/420
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/kansasrrs.pdf (table 53 "Leavenworth Western Branch (UP)", mileposts from Leavenworth Union Station)
research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (UP Table 18; station index, Idana) - used only for the undrawn post-1935 service
metadata.ownership_split: Split per Rule 4: Kansas Central own operation to 1881 (Gould's 13 Nov 1879 purchase was a stock purchase; the road ran as an associated line under L. T. Smith, and the 1880 Missouri Pacific lease was voided) -> Union Pacific 1882 (operation from 31 Dec 1881 / 1 Jan 1882) -> Kansas Central under court Special Master 1895-1896 -> Leavenworth, Kansas and Western 1897-1907 (possession 1 Oct 1897) -> Union Pacific 1908-1934 (purchase 25 May 1908). All whole-line features share identical geometry; Kansas Central construction-stage features share the same vertices clipped to each stage.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn (Rule 1): Leavenworth - Knox (3.0 mi) as freight trackage on UP's Leavenworth Branch after Jan 1935; Clay Center - Miltonvale between the last confirmed passenger year and its 1962-64 abandonment. Unbuilt charter branches (Netawaka, Sabetha, St. Marys, Manhattan, Topeka) and the LK&W's 1897 Colorado extension plan: nothing to draw.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable: steam from opening day; nothing trimmed.
not_yet_sourced: Gauge conversion date conflicts: utahrails gives 25 Aug 1890 (noting other sources 1889-1892); Crimmins gives "about 1893 by the Union Pacific", and his narrative has the 1891 Railroad Commissioners and a Kansas Supreme Court decision (July Term 1892, vol. 47) still disputing the rail for the conversion. Gauge does not affect drawn years; unresolved.

Operator Oct 1893 - Dec 1894: UP entered receivership 13 Oct 1893; whether UP receivers or a separate Kansas Central receiver ran the trains before the 31 Dec 1894 Special Master appointment is not established. Drawn as UP through 1894; Kansas Central (Special Master) 1895-1896. The operator 1 Feb - 1 Oct 1897 is likewise undocumented (drawn as LK&W).

LK&W independence 1897-1908: Crimmins describes a separate company that "decided to re-consolidate with the Union Pacific" in 1908, with its own officers, rolling stock and Railroad Commissioners' reports; utahrails calls it "reorganized as a Union Pacific subsidiary". Drawn in its own colour because the trains ran in its name; a later editor may prefer UP colour if UP managed it day to day.
LK&W sale date: 25 Jun 1897 (Crimmins, auction to Horn & Joyce) vs 24 Sep 1897 (utahrails); possession 1 Oct 1897 either way.

Report block [8] NOT DRAWN: Union Pacific Junction City - Concordia trains over the ex-LK&W Clay Center - Miltonvale track after the 1935 closure. Only one snapshot (Feb 1952 Official Guide UP Table 18, schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951 / 20 Jan 1952; Idana undaggered in the station index) - a 1951 [ANCHOR][OPEN] at best. Start between 1935 and 1951 and end after 1952 (before the 1962-64 abandonment) are unknown. Next sources: utahrails UP Kansas Division ETTs 1950 (No. 10) and 1956 (No. 23).
Holton - Circleville passenger start: track at Circleville Aug/Sep 1877, but no dated 1877 passenger train; drawn from 1878.
Onaga arrival 2 Dec 1877 (one web source) vs early 1878 (Crimmins, utahrails); drawn 1878.
Abandonment application 1 Jul 1933 (utahrails, abandonedrails) vs 11 Jul 1934 (Crimmins); passenger end 1934 either way.

Headways are estimates between snapshots: 2/day each way 1872-74, 1/day 1874-80, 3/day Leavenworth - Garrison 1884 (1/day west of Garrison), 1 mixed/day 1891, tri-weekly mixed June 1934. avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.
The 1872-1888 Leavenworth depot of the Kansas Central is not located; every era draws the 1888 Union Station terminal.
Fowler table 53 shows no z/a/b/c/d (1893-1951) service letters for LK&W stations in the extracted text - possibly a pdftotext layout loss; a visual check of the PDF page may add mid-period anchors.

properties.geometry_quality: Leavenworth - Holton: traced 54.6 mi against 55.4 mi documented (Fowler/branchline.uk Kansas table 53 mileposts from Leavenworth Union Station; Crimmins gives the whole line as 165.39 mi), -1%. Whole-line trace by source: 85.0 mi on OSM ways named for this road (railway=abandoned/razed/dismantled 'Leavenworth, Kansas, and Western RR' 29.1, 'Kansas Central Railroad, LKW, UP (abd 1935)' 28.7, 'Leavenworth, Kansas, & Western (Kansas Central) RR' 23.3, 'Leavenworth, Kansas, & Western RR' 3.9); 52.9 mi on OHM ways 202420094 and 202375580 'Kansas Central Railroad' (Holton - Onaga - Garrison, OHM dates 1878-1934); 18.5 mi on OSM 'Union Pacific RR (Abnd)' Clay Center - Miltonvale (the same track, abandoned 1964); 8.0 mi at the Leavenworth end on unnamed OHM railway ways 202209466/202209468/202209465 (USGS-topo sourced, OHM start 1886/1900) from the Union Depot west and north-west to the start of the named LK&W grade - assumed, not proven, to be the Leavenworth - Knox approach; about 1.5 mi of short joins on other ways (Doodlebug Walking Trail and ATSF Atchison District 0.7 mi at Valley Falls, UP Kansas Subdivision and an unnamed abandoned way 0.6 mi at Onaga, Choctaw Street 0.1 mi at Leavenworth, router connectors 0.2 mi). The opstrace report counted 104.1 mi as '(untagged)' only because the named OSM ways entered its graph from the rail tiles without an old_railway_operator tag; a per-edge audit gives the breakdown above. No straight-line approximated legs within this feature: every leg was routed over mapped track, grade, trail or OHM ways. Waypoint offsets from the drawn line (km): Leavenworth Union Station 0.1, Easton 0.2, Winchester 0.3, Valley Falls 0.4, Half Mound 0.2, Arrington 1.5, Holton 0.9, Circleville 0.2, Soldier 0.6, Havensville 0.3, Onaga 0.1, Wheaton 0.0, Blaine 0.2, Fostoria 0.2, Olsburg 0.2, Garrison (historic, under Tuttle Creek) 0.0, Walsburg 1.4, Leonardville 0.2, Lasita 0.1, Green 0.1, Clay Center 0.3, Idana 0.1, Browndale 0.2, Miltonvale 0.6. Alignment: the line was built 3 ft gauge and converted to standard gauge (1890 per utahrails, c.1893 per Crimmins) on the same roadbed - no relocation is known, so the one surviving grade is drawn for every era. Two era caveats: (1) the east terminal is Leavenworth Union Station (opened 1888), Fowler's milepost 0; the 1872-1888 Kansas Central depot is not located, so pre-1888 years draw a later terminal approach; (2) Garrison and the Big Blue crossing lie under Tuttle Creek Reservoir (1962), so the leg into Garrison follows OHM's reconstruction and the Garrison pin is approximate. This feature draws only Leavenworth - Holton, the extent open 1872-1877; later extensions are separate features so the map never shows track west of Holton before it was open.

segments.note: Kansas Central Railway (3 ft gauge), own operation. Track reached Grasshopper (Valley Falls) Falls 20 Jun 1872 and the first regular schedule began, daily except Sunday; track reached Holton 11 Aug 1872 and regular Holton - Leavenworth service began 2 Sep 1872, two trains each way daily except Sunday (Crimmins 1954 citing local press). Holton was the western terminus 1872-1877. Leavenworth - Valley Falls opened about ten weeks before Valley Falls - Holton, both in 1872, so one feature covers both. headway_min is an estimate from the report's timetable snapshots, not a counted figure for every year in the span.
sources: Segment-level: Crimmins 1954 (track to Grasshopper Falls 20 Jun 1872, first regular schedule; Holton service from 2 Sep 1872, two trains each way); utahrails kansas-central.php

segments.note: Kansas Central, own operation: cut to one train each way 13 Mar 1874 (Crimmins). Holton marked as terminus in the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler table 53 "y" marks) - an independent anchor for 1875. Jay Gould bought the road 13 Nov 1879 and conveyed it to the Union Pacific, but it kept running as an associated line under L. T. Smith's management (Crimmins); UP took over operation 31 Dec 1881 / 1 Jan 1882, so this feature ends 1881. Foreclosure and reorganization as the Kansas Central Railroad (14-15 Apr 1879) did not change the operation. headway_min is an estimate from the report's timetable snapshots, not a counted figure for every year in the span.
sources: Segment-level: Crimmins 1954 (13 Mar 1874 cut to one train each way; 1879 sale/Gould purchase; UP takeover 1 Jan 1882); branchline.uk Kansas table 53 (1875 Official Guide terminus mark at Holton); utahrails (UP assumed operation 31 Dec 1881)

segments.note: Kansas Central, own operation (UP-owned from Nov 1879 but still run under L. T. Smith). Construction resumed June 1877; track at Circleville Aug/Sep 1877 (Crimmins; utahrails Sept 1877) and at Onaga "early months of 1878" (Crimmins, utahrails; one web source says 2 Dec 1877). No dated passenger train beyond Holton is found for 1877, so the span starts 1878, the first year a train demonstrably ran to Onaga; if an 1877 Circleville notice is found, Holton - Circleville could move to 1877. Onaga got the shops and roundhouse. Ends 1881: UP operation from 1 Jan 1882. headway_min is an estimate from the report's timetable snapshots, not a counted figure for every year in the span. One train each way assumed as on the rest of the line after 1874.
sources: Segment-level: Crimmins 1954 (Circleville 1877, Onaga early 1878); utahrails kansas-central.php (Sept 1877, early 1878). Headway NOT sourced for this section.

Dillon, appointed after the 31 Dec 1894 foreclosure suit "to operate the Kansas Central ... until February 1, 1897" (Crimmins). Colour and company follow the Kansas Central because the court, not the UP receivers, ran the trains. Flag: who ran the trains Oct 1893 - Dec 1894 is not established, and the start of the Special Master's actual operation is dated only by his appointment. The interval 1 Feb - 1 Oct 1897 (between the Special Master's term and LK&W possession) is drawn under the LK&W feature. Headway (one mixed train a day, as in 1891) is an estimate.

segments.note: Leavenworth, Kansas and Western Railway. Sold at auction 1897 (25 Jun 1897 to Horn & Joyce per Crimmins; 24 Sep 1897 per utahrails) and took possession 1 Oct 1897; own officers and rolling stock (1906 roster: one passenger and five freight locomotives, three first-class coaches, two combines - Crimmins). 1906 local papers report LK&W excursions to Leavenworth. Treated as its own operator (Crimmins: a separate company that in 1908 "decided to re-consolidate with the Union Pacific"); utahrails calls it a UP subsidiary - see metadata. Sold to the UP 25 May 1908; 1908 is drawn under UP. Includes Feb - Sep 1897 after the Special Master's term ended, whose operator is not separately documented. Headway (one train a day) is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Crimmins 1954 (1897 sale, 1 Oct 1897 possession, 1906 roster and excursions, 25 May 1908 sale); utahrails kansas-central.php (24 Sep 1897 sale). Headway NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: Union Pacific "Leavenworth Western Branch" from the 25 May 1908 purchase (county injunction 28 Jul 1908 later withdrawn). Onaga made the division point between Leavenworth and Miltonvale in 1911 (Onaga local history - source not checked). Service in the final period was by mixed trains ("two 'Daily Except Sunday' mixeds" per utahrails). One train each way daily is an estimate. UP applied to abandon Knox - Clay Center 1 Jul 1933 (utahrails, ICC FD 10060) or 11 Jul 1934 (Crimmins).
sources: Segment-level: Crimmins 1954 (25 May 1908 sale); utahrails kansas-central.php (daily-except-Sunday mixeds). Headway is an estimate, NOT SOURCED year by year.

segments.note: Union Pacific mixed trains, cut to three a week each way in June 1934 (Holton Recorder 7 Jun 1934, via Crimmins). ICC Finance Docket 10060 approved abandonment 8 Oct 1934; the last service ran 10 Jan 1935 (Crimmins, utahrails). 1935 is not drawn: ten days of service do not make a passenger year. Rule 1: Leavenworth - Knox (3.0 mi) stayed as freight trackage on UP's Leavenworth Branch and is NOT drawn after 1934; Clay Center - Miltonvale later carried UP Junction City - Concordia trains (one 1951-52 snapshot only) - not drawn, see metadata not_yet_sourced. headway 3360 min = tri-weekly, applies from June 1934.
sources: Segment-level: Crimmins 1954 citing Holton Recorder 7 Jun 1934 (tri-weekly mixed) and the 10 Jan 1935 last service; abandonedrails (ICC FD 10060, approved 8 Oct 1934)
